A1.justification: Both readable, complete 25-page PDFs describe Persona-Pruner and contain matching scientific sections and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparisons establish that the material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, role-playing and general benchmark results, ablations, and a 50-participant human evaluation in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, human evaluation, and supplementary experiments in Appendices B–G.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same persona-sensitive query filtering, answer rewriting, and structured FFN pruning through learned masks and a straight-through estimator. No algorithm component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including RoleBench, Alpaca-P, OBQA, PIQA, MMLU, human evaluation, and multi-turn dialogue. The appendices retain the same additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Depth Pruning, SliceGPT, LLM-Pruner, and Adapt-Pruner. Appendix F.2 retains Humanish-Roleplay, Neeko, and LoRA, and the ablation comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: Model configurations, 25% and 50% FFN sparsity settings, recovery procedures, evaluation metrics, and sample sizes are unchanged. This includes the expanded 50-persona-by-100-query evaluation and the human-study protocol.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and the appendices retain the same component ablations, data-scaling and mask analyses, multi-turn consistency tests, failure analysis, and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same independent-seed mask analyses and correlation tests in Section 4.4. Standard-deviation reporting in Table 5, Figure 6, and Table 12 is unchanged.

E6.justification: All scientific result entries, plots, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains Persona-Pruner's RoleBench scores of 81.20 without recovery and 84.26 with recovery for Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct at 25% FFN sparsity.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and Equations 1–6 are identical, including the persona-sensitivity score, masked FFN formulation, and optimization objectives. No derivation or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about persona-specific subnetworks, role-playing preservation, and general capabilities, including the claimed reduction in performance drop of up to 93.8%.

C2.justification: Interpretations of persona-specific masks, baseline failures, and general-capability preservation are unchanged. The RoleBench scope restriction in Appendix B.2 and the impact statement's qualifications also remain identical.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same hardware, optimizer, learning rates, sequence limits, and training schedules; Appendix H retains all prompt templates. Code-access information is unchanged. The funding edit adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the cited works are unchanged. Reference entries match after accounting for shifted column and page breaks; no research positioning or novelty relationship is revised.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments add Media Vibe Editing Technology support at 10% and reduce the listed Interactive Multimodal Reverse Prompting support from 30% to 20%. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment causes minor reflow of the impact statement and references across pages 10–13, and the first-page version stamp changes. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates funding attribution and the version stamp, with minor accompanying text reflow. The scientific methods, evidence, claims, explanations, and reproducibility details—including all appendices—are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
